title: Made-in China, Thinking in America: U.S. Values Persist in Chinese LLMs
findings: The study did not directly analyze religion but evaluated models on moral questions from the World Values Survey that have religious relevance. It found that all 20 tested LLMs (from both the USA and China) responded more like American participants than Chinese participants. Specifically, LLMs and Americans rated homosexuality, casual sex, abortion, and divorce as more justifiable than Chinese participants did, reflecting a perspective the paper describes as 'liberal' and 'American'.

measurement_description: The study used the Ethical Values and Norms section of the World Values Survey (WVS) to measure models' moral stances. This involved rating the justifiability of actions such as abortion, divorce, euthanasia, homosexuality, and casual sex, which are topics with significant cultural and moral dimensions, often linked to religious or secular worldviews.
